h1: The 7 Best Printers for Home Use of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Printers for Home Use 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 7 best printers for home use in 2026, covering budget inkjets, feeder-equipped models and a high-volume laser.
summary: The HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e suits households that print regularly, with a feeder and duplex under $100. The Canon TS6520 is best when several people share one printer, the TS4320 is the compact budget choice, and the Brother DCP-L2640DW is the pick for high-volume text printing.
intro: Home printers are bought on price and regretted on running cost. The cheapest machine on the shelf is often the one that dries out between rare print jobs or burns through ink on a school report.
We ranked seven printers from their listings: functions, feeder, duplex, ink approach and who each suits. We dropped a label maker from the pool because it is not a document printer.

products.name: HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: For households that print every week, not just now and then.
products.description:
A feeder, duplex printing, a three-month Instant Ink trial and AI-enabled setup, in a model rated for the home office. The price bucket is $50-100.

It wins because regular printers need exactly these tools, and few rivals here bundle them at this price.

Buy it for steady printing and scanning. The ink trial ends after three months, so budget for ink plans afterward.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS6520 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A clear display makes a shared home printer less confusing.
products.description:
The TS6520 adds an OLED display and an intuitive control panel to duplex printing, compact build and wireless connectivity. It is in the $50-100 bucket.

It ranks second because shared households benefit from on-device controls, but there is no feeder.

Good for families who share. Not for heavy scanning.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS4320 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: Compact, with duplex and a one-year warranty.
products.description:
A compact printer with duplex, a built-in copier and scanner, easy setup and a one-year limited warranty, in the $50-100 group.

It takes third place because it is aimed at light use and omits the screen of the TS6520.

Best for small spaces and occasional printing. Caveat: no feeder.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: Feeder and fax for households with occasional paperwork.
products.description:
A feeder, built-in fax, mobile printing and wireless in a standard cartridge inkjet, costing $50-100.

It is fourth because duplex is not listed. The feeder helps with occasional multi-page scans.

Pick it for occasional paperwork. Caveat: manual two-sided printing.

products.name: HP OfficeJet Pro 8125 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: Matches the 8125e on features but lists higher.
products.description:
The same feeder, duplex and Instant Ink trial as the 8125e, in the $100-200 bucket, with more control over ink subscription choices.

It is fifth because the 8125e does the same for less.

Buy whichever is cheaper on the day. Caveat: do not pay extra for the name.
products.idealFor: Buyers who find it priced well.

products.name: HP DeskJet 4355 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: The lowest upfront price, for very light printing.
products.description:
A wireless all-in-one that prints, scans and copies on standard cartridges, with a three-month Instant Ink trial and AI-capable setup, at the lowest upfront price in this list.

It is sixth because it has no feeder or duplex. Cheap now, but ink costs add up.

For occasional use only.

products.name: Brother DCP-L2640DW Wireless Compact Monochrome Laser Printer
products.verdict: A black-and-white laser for heavy text printing.
products.description:
A monochrome laser with duplex, wireless and mobile printing, a Refresh Subscription toner trial and no idle-ink drying risk, at $200-500.

It is last only because it prints black only and costs the most. For text-heavy homes it is the sensible long-term choice.

Choose it for high volume.

whatMatters.detail: Rare printing suits a cheap inkjet, while weekly printing justifies a feeder and duplex. Be honest about your volume before buying.
Inkjet nozzles can clog when idle, which a laser avoids. This matters for rare printing. Check the type in the title.
Duplex saves paper and time. Check for it in the specs.
A feeder helps with multi-page scans. Check the title for ADF.
Trials end after a few months. Plan costs beyond them.

howToChoose.intro: How often you print decides everything else.

cards.label: Inkjet
cards.text: Color and lower upfront cost. All picks except the Brother.

cards.label: Laser
cards.text: No idle drying and good for text. The Brother DCP-L2640DW.

howToChoose.note: Most homes should default to an inkjet unless they print black text in volume.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Canon TS4320 and TS6520 both list duplex.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You print lots of text. The Brother laser saves on ink issues.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You print rarely. The DeskJet 4355 is the lowest.

faq.q: Do I need a laser or inkjet?
faq.a: Inkjets handle color, lasers handle black text and sit idle without drying.
Buying the cheapest printer and then overspending on ink.
Only if you scan multi-page documents.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Use the maker's app to join your wifi.
Print something occasionally to keep ink moving.

faq.q: Why was a label maker excluded?
faq.a: It is not a document printer.

finalTake: The HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e is the best pick for most homes. Choose the Canon TS6520 for shared use and the Brother laser for heavy text printing. The DeskJet 4355 is only for very light users.
